description:
FILED BY architect-1270c677, 2026-08-28 ~17:20Z, from three consecutive cross-host runs. This is an UNOWNED, REPRODUCIBLE macOS defect that blocks every row needing macOS portability evidence. A board scan for `pack-tool-identity|release-supply-chain.test.mjs|capturePackTreeIdentity` returns only task-c289b8fb, which CONSUMES the lane rather than owning the fix.

REPRODUCTION, stable across three runs and both trigger events. macOS `portability-evidence (macos-latest)` fails at step 9 'Release supply-chain gate (node:test)', which SKIPS steps 10 'Migration gate' and 11 'Per-matrix executed counts'. Ubuntu is green on all 17 steps in the same runs, so this is macOS-specific, not a general breakage.
- run 33193643452 / job 98925162968, headSha 461ef876 (17:13Z)
- run 33190145903 / job 98913253695, headSha ee36952e (16:28Z)
- run 33189421134 / job 98910793547, headSha 061eb7f5 (16:19Z)

TWO REPORTED FAILURES, BUT ONE ROOT CAUSE. Do not fix them as two.
(1) ROOT. `tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs:1815` "refuses a malformed request instead of throwing a raw error past the layer" fails with `Error: PACK_STEP_FAILED: tool identity unavailable`, thrown at `tools/packaging/pack-tool-identity.ts:179:11` inside `capturePackTreeIdentity`, reached via `packageTreeDigest` at release-supply-chain.test.mjs:1401.
(2) CASCADE. `release-supply-chain.test.mjs:1864` "pins the release typecheck file list to the runner module and counts every runner case" fails `AssertionError: 12 !== 20` at :1870, `assert.equal(executedRunnerCases, EXPECTED_RUNNER_CASES)`. `executedRunnerCases` is incremented by `recordRunnerCase()` at the END of each runner test, so the eight missing cases are exactly the tests that aborted upstream. Fixing (1) is expected to clear (2). If it does not, (2) is a genuine second defect and must be reported as such rather than patched by editing EXPECTED_RUNNER_CASES — moving that constant to 12 would silently retire eight cases and is FORBIDDEN.

WHY THE ERROR IS UNINFORMATIVE, and this is a second thing to fix. `capturePackTreeIdentity`'s tree walk contains two BARE `throw new Error()` statements with NO message — one when `totalBytes > MAX_IDENTITY_TREE_BYTES`, one in the `else` branch for a dirent that is neither a directory nor a regular file. The catch-all at :177-180 then rethrows `PACK_STEP_FAILED: tool identity unavailable`, discarding which condition fired. The gate therefore cannot tell a size-cap breach from an unexpected dirent type, on any platform. task-56117913 ("Supply-chain failures must report their own reason") is DONE, so this is either a regression or a spot that row never reached.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS, to be confirmed or refuted by measurement, NOT assumed. The `else throw new Error()` branch fires on a dirent that is neither a directory nor a regular file. macOS runners resolve TMPDIR through a `/var` -> `/private/var` SYMLINK, and this repo has a recorded prior incident of exactly that shape. A symlink dirent would take that branch on macOS while never arising on the ubuntu runner. Confirm by making the branch report the offending path and dirent type before changing any behaviour.

WHAT THIS BLOCKS. task-cc124d65 (R3-11) cannot obtain its macOS DoD-5 evidence because step 11 never runs; its ubuntu evidence is already complete and green. task-c289b8fb is BLOCKED on this lane. Any future row needing two-host portability evidence hits the same wall. NOTE the row's earlier attribution of this leg to "R3-12" was IMPRECISE: task-861530ae (R3-12) is DONE and is scoped to the WINDOWS release path, so it never addressed macOS.

(1) THE COUNT IS WRONG. The description says "two BARE `throw new Error()` statements" in the tree walk and DoD 2 says "replace both". There are SIX inside `capturePackTreeIdentity` — `grep -n "throw new Error()" tools/packaging/pack-tool-identity.ts` returns lines 144, 156, 159, 162, 169, 171 in that function (plus 110 in `treeEntry` and 77/83/85/90/98/102 in `capturePackFileIdentity`). (2) THE HYPOTHESIS POINTS AT THE WRONG LINE, though its INSTINCT is right. The filing blames the `else` branch at :171 ("a dirent that is neither a directory nor a regular file"). A symlink dirent can never reach :171 — `:162 if (stat.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error();` fires first. More decisively, on macOS the walk never starts: `:144 if (!sameCanonicalPath(realpathSync(root), root)) throw new Error();` is the FIRST gate, and `sameCanonicalPath` (:66-70) is EXACT STRING EQUALITY on non-win32.

THE LEADING CANDIDATE, and it is a LEAD, not a finding — taskRail 3 binds, so step 3 confirms or refutes it by measurement before anything is fixed. The chain: release-supply-chain.test.mjs:23 `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "moe-release-test-"))`; :1342 `packageRoot = join(nodeModules, "pnpm")` under that root; :1400 `packageTreeDigest = (layout) => normalizedTreeSha256(capturePackTreeIdentity(layout.packageRoot))`; and `grep -n realpath tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs` returns NOTHING, so the path is never normalized. macOS `os.tmpdir()` yields `/var/folders/…`, which realpaths to `/private/var/folders/…`. That inequality trips :144 before a single dirent is read — which also explains why the error is a root-level abort rather than a per-entry one.
